Writ Petition No. 189 of 1976.
In the matter of an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.
lawyer:
S. R. Pail with S.C Das & Zakir Ahmed  -----For the Petitioner. 
Syed J. R. Mudadsir Hossain -----For Respondents No. 1 & 2.
parties:
Srimongal Pourashava ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
Bangladesh through the Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms & others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment: 3. In this connection reference may be made to the provisions of Hats and Bazars (Establishment) and Acquisition Ordinance 1959 (Ordinance No XIX of 1959). Sub-section (1) of section 2 of the said Ordinance provides that no person shall establish any hats and bazars except without a license for that purpose from the Collector in such form as may be prescribed by rules. Sub-section (2) of section 2 of the Ordinance provides that any hats and bazars established in contravention of the aforesaid provisions shall be forfeited to the Government. Hats and Bazars (Establishment) and Acquisition (Amendment) Act of 1966 (Act XII/67) had amended the provisions of section 2 of the aforesaid Ordinance No. XIX of 1959 where under at present no person shall establish any hats or bazars excepting the Government or any local authority with the approval of the Government The local authority means local-councils as defined in sub clause (24) of clause 1 of Article 3 of the Basic Democracy Ordinance of 1959 and subsequently it included a Municipal Committee under the Municipal Administration Ordinance 1960 followed by the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977. Subsequently Bangladesh Government Hats and Bazars (Management) Order of 1972 (P.O. 73/72) was introduced providing for the management of all Government hats and bazars. P.O. No. 73 of 1972 stood repealed by Bangladesh Government Hats and bazars (Management Repeal) Ordinance 1975 (Ordinance No. 59 of 1975). Considering the aforesaid provisions of law it now appears that there is no special provisions for management of Government hats and Bazars but the Government has an absolute right to establish any hat and bazar. A local authority including a Municipality or Pourashava can also establish a hat and bazar with the prior approval of the Government. All the references made to the various provisions of law made herein-before are prospective in nature providing for powers of the Government and any local authority including a Pourashava to establish and to maintain any hat or bazar or a market as the case may be after the promulgation of the laws referred to hereinbefore. The aforesaid statutes are completely silent with regard to the powers of the Government to take over such hats and bazars and markets in possession of a local authority like a Pourashava. It appears that apart front the general provisions of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 there is no other special statutory provisions authorising the Government to acquire and to take over any hat and bazar and market already remaining under the ownership and possession of a local authority and a Pourashava.
